column2: This is just a rebranding of novelty bias to make it seem like a new idea

The earliest reference on Wikipedia is 2011, but I was saying "Shiny Object Syndrome" and even specifically abbreviating it "SOS" by at least 2005.

I know that I first heard it from somewhere else, but I do not remember where. I'm pretty sure it was a TV show.

Does any one remember where it originated from?

"Shiny object syndrome is the situation ..."

'The situation'? Can't help but feel this is very imprecise and unserious language.
I call it Toddler Soccer Syndrome. Ball's over there? Let's all chase it. Oh, moved over here now? Everyone run the other way.
They're just letting anyone make a Wikipedia page these days huh
Why is such a small article being upvoted? It's basically just a definition page.
If anything, there's so much new stuff these days that I don't even get the FOMO to try it all.. building it myself is easy too.
In boardgame communities, it’s called “Cult of the New”.
I wonder if this has any relevance at all to a bunch of new stuff that people on HN seem very obsessed over these days.

An aspect of this I find interesting is that previously effort was a reasonably good barrier to making something new. If a feature/library existed someone cared enough to put the work in to make it exist.

Now it’s just a question of tokens. The presentation/feature list is no sign of effort or caring. So we get limitless new shiny things to try and filter through
